sections.title: Exercises
sections.body:
**Exercise 1 — Cancellable drafter.** Add a `KeyboardInterrupt` handler to the Live Email Drafter that, on Ctrl+C, stops streaming and prints whatever has been rendered so far as the final draft. Test by interrupting mid-stream.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

Wrap the `for chunk in chain.stream(...)` loop in a `try/except KeyboardInterrupt`. The `rendered` variable already holds whatever has been streamed — just break and return it. Add a `console.print("[red]Interrupted.[/]")` message for clarity.
</details>

**Exercise 2 — Token-level streaming with `iter()`.** Inside `summarize_live`, when you hit a `ModelRequestNode`, use `node.stream(run.ctx)` to stream partial text to the panel. Render each chunk as it arrives.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

Replace the event-append branch for `is_model_request_node` with: `async with node.stream(run.ctx) as response_stream: async for chunk in response_stream.stream_text(): events.append(f"[dim]{chunk!r}[/]"); live.update(...)`. The exact method name varies by Pydantic AI version — check `dir(response_stream)` if `stream_text` isn't present. This is the bridge between event streaming and token streaming.
</details>

**Exercise 3 — WebSockets for production.** Replace the `rich.live` rendering in either project with a FastAPI WebSocket endpoint that streams chunks to a browser client. The browser renders chunks into a `<pre>` element as they arrive.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

`pip install fastapi uvicorn`. Define `@app.websocket("/stream")` that awaits chunks from an async generator wrapping `chain.astream(...)` (note the `a` prefix for async). On the frontend, `const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8000/stream"); ws.onmessage = e => pre.textContent += e.data;`. This is the foundation of every chat UI you've ever used.
</details>
